articles.title: Really? New York stadium named the best place in America for food
articles.standfirst: Surprisingly, an MLB team based in New York has come in at No. 1 on a stadium food ranking.
articles.summary: Surprisingly, an MLB team based in New York has come in at No. 1 on a stadium food ranking.
articles.body:
When it comes to actually winning baseball games, there's only one MLB team that's actually been doing that consistently as of late: the New York Yankees . Unfortunately, the New York Mets can't say the same.

But there's one thing the Mets can say they do much better than the Yankees: Stadium food . Yelp recently ranked the Top 50 stadiums across the United States for gameday food , in all major sports, and Citi Field came in at No. 1 on the list.

Citi Field ranked as the best stadium for gameday eats in America by Yelp

Yelp had this to say about Citi Field, which features a large variety of different foods.

The concourse at Citi Field mirrors Queens itself, fast, lively, and full of surprises worth stopping for. This year’s 37 new menu items span 27 vendor partnerships, with The Queensboro’s Kimchi Reuben earning its place among the must-tries — house-cured corned beef, kimchi fennel, and Russian dressing stacked on toasted rye. For the bold and hungriest eaters, Willets Point Brewery’s 9-9-9 Challenge offers nine mini Nathan’s hot dogs and nine 4-ounce pours across nine innings, which is the kind of thing you sign up for confidently in the first inning and deeply reconsider by the fifth. With a spread this extensive, it makes sense that some Yelpers say 'I was really [just] there for the food.'

There are several enticing eats all around the stadium. While Shake Shack is one of the most notable restaurants there, Adam Richman's Burger Hall of Fame takes most of the plaudits when it comes to burgers.

There are also spots for Jamaican patties, BBQ, lobster rolls, sushi , and much more. Certainly, there are no shortage of different cuisines to choose from when visiting for a Mets home game.

Citi Field also features tons of alternative options for people with specific eating diets or habits. They have vegan and gluten friendly options, as well as kosher and vegetarian options.

articles.title: Mets legend Ron Darling blasts Juan Soto over lack of effort: "You end up being embarrassed"
articles.standfirst: The SNY analyst questioned Soto's hustle for a second consecutive game, although the Mets star later showed his health may not be preventing him from running hard
articles.summary: The SNY analyst questioned Soto's hustle for a second consecutive game, although the Mets star later showed his health may not be preventing him from running hard
articles.body:
J uan Soto 's effort has become a talking point during the Mets ' Subway Series against the Yankees , and longtime New York broadcaster Ron Darling was not prepared to overlook another slow start out of the batter's box.

Soto was criticized during Saturday's game at Yankee Stadium after failing to immediately sprint down the first-base line following a ground ball to second. The play ultimately ended in an out, but Anthony Volpe 's bobble briefly gave Soto an opportunity to reach safely.

Darling , who was calling the game for SNY, acknowledged the defensive mistake but argued that Soto's initial lack of urgency was what put him in the difficult position.

"If you’re not going to run, things like that are going to happen," Darling said on SNY. "Bobbled. If you don’t run out of the box, then you end up being embarrassed. DHing today because last night, I don’t know what his physical ailments are; he can’t play left field in this ballpark right now."

The criticism came less than 24 hours after another controversial sequence involving Soto during Friday night's 6-4 loss to the Yankees.

Soto appeared slow to react to a Ryan McMahon single to left field in the eighth inning, allowing another run to score and helping New York extend its advantage. The Mets ultimately lost the opener of the three-game Subway Series.

The back-to-back incidents have raised questions about whether Soto is still dealing with the effects of the calf problems that have disrupted his season.

Soto's calf injuries add another layer to the controversy

The 27-year-old has spent significant time on the injured list in 2026. A right calf strain sidelined him for roughly two and a half weeks in April, while a Grade 2 strain to his left calf later kept him out for 31 games during July and August.

Soto eventually returned on August 29 after missing five weeks with the left calf injury. He immediately contributed in a 6-2 victory over the Houston Astros, collecting an RBI single in his first game back.

Those injuries make the discussion about effort more complicated. A player returning from significant calf trouble may understandably be cautious about explosive movements, particularly when running from a standing position or chasing a ball in the outfield.

Gary Cohen raised precisely that possibility during the SNY broadcast.

"He had two balls drop in front of him last night. If you do the math, it might have cost the Mets the game," the play-by-play broadcaster said.

Cohen also pointed toward the injuries Soto has suffered to "both calves" this season as a potential explanation for what viewers were seeing.

However, Saturday's game provided evidence that Soto can still run effectively when necessary.

Earlier in the contest, the Mets star hustled into second for a double, tagged up at third and eventually scored on a Carson Benge single. Keith Hernandez, another former Mets star working the broadcast, praised Soto's movement on the play.

"He showed no issues with his calf," Keith Henrndez said. "He ran like the devil on that double."

Soto then added an even bigger contribution in the seventh inning, launching a mammoth solo home run to extend the Mets ' lead to 6-2.

The contrasting sequences underline why the issue has become such a prominent topic. Soto has demonstrated that he is capable of running aggressively, yet his lack of immediate effort on certain plays has drawn criticism from the Mets ' broadcast team.

For a player carrying a record-setting $765 million contract, the scrutiny is inevitable. Soto joined the Mets after signing the massive 15-year deal ahead of the 2025 season, putting enormous expectations on his every at-bat and defensive opportunity.

The Mets also need their superstar healthy and productive as they attempt to remain in contention late in the season. New York entered the Subway Series at 68-78 and had already lost Friday's opener, while the Yankees improved to 85-62 following their victory.

Darling's comments therefore come at a crucial point in the Mets' season. The criticism is not necessarily about one ground ball or one defensive mistake, but about the perception of consistency and effort from one of the most important players on the roster.

Soto has already shown that his calf can withstand significant running when required. The question now is whether he can convince his critics, including members of the Mets ' own broadcast team, that the same urgency will be there on every play as New York pushes toward the postseason.

articles.title: ‘Is he real?’: Mets top prospect Mitch Voit goes viral as fans call him the ‘most attractive person ever’ and suspect he’s AI
articles.standfirst: The Mets prospect has the stats to match the looks
articles.summary: The Mets prospect has the stats to match the looks
articles.body:
Mitch Voit is quickly becoming one of the New York Mets’ most intriguing young players, but his latest wave of attention has come from somewhere completely unexpected.

The 21-year-old infield prospect went viral Monday after video from his media availability at Citi Field circulated widely on social media. Fans became fascinated by Voit’s appearance, with several joking that he looked too polished to be real.

One social media user called Voit the “most attractive person of all time” and compared him to an AI-generated Disney prince. Another joked that the Mets had become the first MLB team to use an AI-generated prospect.

“I’ve said it before, but I’ll say it again: Mitch Voit might be the most attractive person of all time. Dude deadass looks like an AI generated Disney prince,” wrote one person on X.

Others pointed to the combination of his appearance and his impressive statistics, joking that Voit could be equally comfortable on a baseball field or in a cologne advertisement.

The unexpected attention comes during a season in which Voit has established himself as one of the organization’s most promising prospects.

Mitch Voit’s rapid rise through the Mets system

The Mets selected Voit with the 38th overall pick in the 2025 MLB Draft after his standout career at Michigan. He arrived in professional baseball as a two-way player, having played several infield positions while also pitching in college.

New York has since concentrated on his development as a position player. Voit has worked extensively at shortstop this season, adding another position to his already versatile defensive profile. MLB Pipeline ranks him as the Mets’ No. 4 prospect.

His performance has backed up that high ranking. Voit finished the season with a .273 batting average, 13 home runs, 59 RBIs and 45 stolen bases over 105 games between High-A Brooklyn and Double-A Binghamton.

His production became even more impressive as the season progressed. From May 24 through the end of the minor-league campaign, Voit hit .300 with an .866 OPS. Following his promotion to Double-A in late July, he batted .347 with two home runs and a .947 OPS over 29 games.

Those numbers helped earn Voit the Mets’ 2026 Minor League Player of the Year award.

Mets interim manager Andy Green has also highlighted Voit’s mindset.

“You don’t worry about people who are wired that way,” Green said Monday.

“You believe in people who are wired that way, that continue to do the right thing, regardless of how tough the circumstances get, because the circumstances get a lot tougher [in the major leagues].”

Voit says his focus is on understanding his strengths, identifying how they match up against each pitcher and getting the most out of every at-bat.

That approach could help him continue climbing toward the major leagues.

Alongside Voit’s growing reputation as a legitimate Mets prospect, he’s become an internet sensation among fans who still can't quite believe he looks like a real person.

articles.title: The Mets, the $1 billion team, have become the embarrassment of MLB after allowing a double
articles.standfirst: New York slumped to their 83rd loss of the season in a 7-1 defeat to the Baltimore Orioles.
articles.summary: New York slumped to their 83rd loss of the season in a 7-1 defeat to the Baltimore Orioles.
articles.body:
The New York Mets have spent heavily to build a roster capable of competing at the highest level, but their latest collapse offered an awkward reminder that money cannot prevent basic mistakes as a routine fly ball exposed costly confusion.

With the highly paid and highly regarded trio of Juan Soto , Francisco Lindor and Bo Bichette converging on a ball in shallow left, none of the three took charge as the ball dropped for a leadoff double.

The poor defensive play drew immediate criticism from the ESPN broadcast as the Mets fell further behind whilst booing broke out, and Kevin Brown did not hold back when describing the play.

“The ball will drop,” Brown said. “Lindor, Bichette and Soto, about a billion-dollars worth of Mets out in left field and none of ’em could pick it up.”

The trio actually represents more than $1.2 billion in contractual value. Soto ’s 15-year deal is worth $765 million and can reach $805 million with incentives, while Lindor is signed for $341 million and Bichette agreed to a $126 million contract.

The mistake was particularly damaging because the fly ball carried an expected batting average of just .010, meaning the ball should be caught 90% of the time whilst Xzavion Curry then surrendered a two-run homer two batters later.

Routine defensive error became a three-run deficit, and the game quickly began slipping away from New York as Soto charged toward the ball whilst Bichette tracked it with his shoulder toward the plate.

Lindor moved diagonally but appeared concerned about colliding with Bichette , who ducked at the last moment, and Eduardo Perez believed he should have made the play, while David Ross agreed.

“Originally, I thought this was Francisco Lindor’s ball,” Perez said, explaining that Bichette was waiting for Lindor to communicate while Soto was the only player who could override everyone.

The result was another defensive breakdown during a four-game losing streak and a five-losses-in-six stretch as the Orioles capitalized immediately.

Taking a 6-0 lead in the second inning before completing a 7-1 victory, the Orioles sealed a three-game sweep and left New York with a bitter taste in their mouths.

The Mets are now facing another disappointing chapter in a season that has unravelled, and is now seemingly going through the motions until the end of the campaign.

Pete Alonso complimentary to Mets fans upon New York return

Meanwhile Pete Alonso ’s return to Citi Field provided one of the few positive storylines during the series as the former Mets slugger hit two home runs, including the 300th of his career, and received a curtain call from the home crowd.

Alonso was also warmly received throughout the series, making his postgame comments particularly intriguing as the Orioles star thanked supporters while also mentioning the New York Yankees and saying the entire city remains meaningful to him.

“I am beyond thankful for all the support and it was really fun to play,” Alonso said. “I feel like New York will always be a place where it feels like homecoming – it doesn't matter whether it's here or at Yankee Stadium.”

The Orioles will visit Yankee Stadium from September 25-27, giving Alonso another opportunity to play in New York .

Meanwhile, the Mets sit 69-83 last in the National League East and 19.5 games behind the division-leading Atlanta Braves .

articles.title: Jared Young health status: A brutal collision knocks the Mets player out, alarming fans
articles.standfirst: Young raised his thumb to the crowd after being struck by teammate Nolan McLean’s knee
articles.summary: Young raised his thumb to the crowd after being struck by teammate Nolan McLean’s knee
articles.body:
A seemingly harmless ground ball brought Thursday night’s Mets -Phillies game to an abrupt halt when Jared Young collided with teammate Nolan McLean and remained face-down on the field for several agonizing moments.

The frightening play unfolded in the top of the sixth inning at Citi Field. Philadelphia’s Justin Crawford rolled a slow grounder up the first-base line, drawing both Young and McLean toward the ball.

Young dove in an attempt to make the play as McLean tried to leap over him. McLean ’s knee appeared to catch Young on the side of the head, sending the first baseman hard into the dirt. Young didn't immediately move.

Players from both clubs gathered nearby as Mets medical personnel rushed onto the field and began treating the 31-year-old. Trainers appeared to stabilize his neck before preparing him to be moved.

Rosenthal offers encouraging update

The game was being broadcast nationally by Fox, with reporter Ken Rosenthal positioned close to the action. As medical staff continued working on Young , Rosenthal relayed the first reassuring signs.

“Obviously a terrible scene here,” Rosenthal said. “But it appears he is speaking. It appears he's got movement on his limbs. You can see right there.”

Young was eventually secured onto a stretcher and taken toward a cart. The crowd responded with a standing ovation, and Young offered one encouraging gesture of his own by raising his thumb as he was taken away from the field.

“They're going to carry him off and take him off on a cart,” Rosenthal said. “Hopefully, Jared Young is okay.”

Mark Vientos replaced Young at first base when play resumed.

The Mets hadn't immediately issued a detailed medical update following the incident. Given the nature of the collision, Young was expected to undergo further evaluation for possible head and neck injuries.

The most encouraging information came from Rosenthal ’s field-level report that Young appeared to be speaking and moving his limbs before leaving the field.

Young has been part of New York’s first-base mix this season and had recently contributed offensively, including a double in the Mets ’ game against Baltimore earlier in the week.

None of that mattered in the immediate aftermath of Thursday’s collision. The sight of Young lying motionless shifted the mood inside Citi Field instantly, and the reaction from both teams reflected the seriousness of the moment.

Until the Mets provide a formal diagnosis, the full extent of Young ’s injury remains unclear. The strongest positive sign came as he raised his thumb toward the crowd after one of the most frightening plays of the Mets ’ season.

articles.title: “Shameful and dangerous”: Medical staff face a wave of criticism over the incident involving Jared Young's stretcher
articles.standfirst: The New York Mets first baseman was hospitalized after a frightening collision.
articles.summary: The New York Mets first baseman was hospitalized after a frightening collision.
articles.body:
Jared Young ’s frightening injury at Citi Field was followed by another uncomfortable scene, as the New York Mets first baseman’s stretcher removal drew sharp criticism.

The 31-year-old was knocked unconscious during the sixth inning when pitcher Nolan McLean ’s knee struck his head as both players converged on a slow grounder near first base.

Young was taken to a hospital after he remained down for several minutes before being stabilized and loaded onto a stretcher.

The Mets later said he had feeling in his extremities, while interim manager Andy Green said a CT scan was fortunately negative.

However, video of the stretcher being moved showed medical personnel struggling with the equipment before he was taken toward the outfield in the game against the Philadelphia Phillies .

The footage prompted viewers to question how the evacuation was handled, sparking an emotional reaction on X.com, formerly Twitter.

One user wrote, “Worked in EMS for years. Coworkers like these people are why I don’t work in EMS anymore. The standards need to be raised.”

Whilst a second added, “As a paramedic, this is tough to watch. You’d think the Mets could spring the bill for an electric Striker cot, but still no excuse for the sloppiness from that crew.”

Players on both sides grateful Young is OK

His injury is especially difficult given his rise this season. After returning from a knee injury that cost him roughly six weeks, he earned a larger role and entered Thursday batting .266 with nine homers and 39 RBIs.

Thursday’s game ended with Philadelphia winning 3-0, but the result was secondary as attention remained fixed on Young .

New York have not currently announced a further diagnosis beyond his concussion symptoms and negative CT scan.

The Mets manager had said he was experiencing concussion symptoms but had full use of his extremities but whilst he was carted off the field, the player raised an arm to reassure fans and players.

Young gave the Citi Field crowd a thumbs-up as he was driven away and that gesture offered a welcome sign after teammates had gathered around him while he lay on the infield dirt.

“It is scary to see one of our brothers,” Francisco Lindor said. “One of the most respected and loved teammates that we have here, like that."

Lindor ’s comment perfectly captured the concern inside the Mets clubhouse, especially for players who have been exposed to such collisions throughout their careers and intimately understand the gravity of the situation.

Likewise for the Phillies , as Bryce Harper also addressed the injury before discussing the game itself in a compassionate and sporting gesture.

“I hope he’s OK, may God be with him and his family," Harper said, post-game.

Young was taken to a hospital after he remained down for several minutes before being stabilized and loaded onto a stretcher.
The Mets later said he had feeling in his extremities, while interim manager Andy Green said a CT scan was fortunately negative.
However, video of the stretcher being moved showed medical personnel struggling with the equipment before he was taken toward the outfield in the game against the Philadelphia Phillies .
The footage prompted viewers to question how the evacuation was handled, sparking an emotional reaction on X.com, formerly Twitter.
One user wrote, “Worked in EMS for years. Coworkers like these people are why I don’t work in EMS anymore. The standards need to be raised.”
Whilst a second added, “As a paramedic, this is tough to watch. You’d think the Mets could spring the bill for an electric Striker cot, but still no excuse for the sloppiness from that crew.”
Players on both sides grateful Young is OK

His injury is especially difficult given his rise this season. After returning from a knee injury that cost him roughly six weeks, he earned a larger role and entered Thursday batting .266 with nine homers and 39 RBIs.
Thursday’s game ended with Philadelphia winning 3-0, but the result was secondary as attention remained fixed on Young .
New York have not currently announced a further diagnosis beyond his concussion symptoms and negative CT scan.
The Mets manager had said he was experiencing concussion symptoms but had full use of his extremities but whilst he was carted off the field, the player raised an arm to reassure fans and players.
Young gave the Citi Field crowd a thumbs-up as he was driven away and that gesture offered a welcome sign after teammates had gathered around him while he lay on the infield dirt.
“It is scary to see one of our brothers,” Francisco Lindor said. “One of the most respected and loved teammates that we have here, like that."

Lindor ’s comment perfectly captured the concern inside the Mets clubhouse, especially for players who have been exposed to such collisions throughout their careers and intimately understand the gravity of the situation.
Likewise for the Phillies , as Bryce Harper also addressed the injury before discussing the game itself in a compassionate and sporting gesture.
“I hope he’s OK, may God be with him and his family," Harper said, post-game.

articles.title: Surprise twist in Queens: Andy Green reverses course and signs 3-year contract with Mets
articles.standfirst: The New York Mets have found their permanent general manager.
articles.summary: The New York Mets have found their permanent general manager.
articles.body:
The New York Mets have made a surprising decision at the end of a disappointing season, removing Andy Green ’s interim tag and committing to him as their manager. Green has agreed to a three-year contract, giving him a chance to lead New York beyond its turbulent 2026 MLB campaign and shape the club’s direction heading into next season.

The decision comes after Green replaced Carlos Mendoza in June and took charge of a team that had fallen out of contention after entering the season with major expectations. And one of the team's star players, Francisco Lindor , believes Green has already established an important connection with the clubhouse since taking over, particularly through his emphasis on accountability and leadership. “I have a lot of respect for Andy,” Lindor told SNY. “I think he’s been good at the role that he’s got right now. Not necessarily the role of managing, because I didn’t see his role this year as to manage. “His role, right now, was to come in and bring light, bring ownership, bring respect, and bring accountability. He’s succeeded at it.” Green ’s appointment comes with the Mets set to miss the postseason for a second straight year, despite carrying one of baseball’s highest-profile rosters and significant financial investment. The club reached the National League Championship Series just two seasons ago, but its ongoing campaign deteriorated badly and forced the organization to reconsider its leadership. Green now inherits a roster that still features major talent, including Juan Soto , while the front office prepares for an offseason centered on restoring consistency and competitiveness. The 49-year-old manager previously held the job with the San Diego Padres from 2016 through 2019, finishing that tenure with a 274-366 record before his dismissal. After leaving San Diego , Green joined the Chicago Cubs as bench coach under David Ross before eventually returning to the Mets organization as a senior vice president for player development before becoming the manager.

Mets receive boost ahead of Texas Rangers clash

New York will open a three-game road series against the Texas Rangers on Tuesday, September 22 before finishing the regular season with three games against the Washington Nationals . The Mets also received a bullpen boost when the team confirmed pitcher Devin Williams was activated from the 15-day injured list after missing roughly six weeks with a right shoulder injury. Williams has posted a 4.66 ERA with 16 saves in 19 appearances during his first season with the organization following his sizable three-year, $51 million contract signed in December 2025. The Mets signed Williams after his season with the New York Yankees , hoping the two-time All-Star and two-time National League Reliever of the Year could anchor a revamped bullpen. His return gives Green another experienced arm to manage during the final week, although Christian Scott was placed on the 15-day injured list with left knee inflammation. Green will now enter the offseason with the certainty of a three-year contract and a much larger task: turning a talented Mets roster into a team capable of returning to October baseball.

articles.title: The Mets bank their future on a manager who has never been to the playoffs
articles.standfirst: The owners had nearly three months watching him manage the team through a disappointing season
articles.summary: The owners had nearly three months watching him manage the team through a disappointing season
articles.body:
At first glance, the New York Mets' decision appears puzzling. On Tuesday, the organization removed Andy Green's interim tag and signed him to a three-year contract, officially making him the club's full-time manager. It is a significant vote of confidence for a baseball lifer whose managerial résumé includes a notable omission: he has never led a team to the postseason.

During his four seasons managing the San Diego Padres from 2016 through 2019, Green never reached October. His coaching stops with the Arizona Diamondbacks and Chicago Cubs also did not result in playoff appearances during his tenure. And although he took over the Mets in June and steadied the club during a difficult season, New York's playoff hopes had largely faded by the time he inherited the job.

So why would a franchise with championship aspirations commit its future to a manager without a postseason appearance on his record? The answer is that the Mets appear to be evaluating Green on more than his October résumé.

The Mets saw enough during the interim run

When Green replaced Carlos Mendoza in late June, he inherited a team that was already dealing with disappointment and underperformance. Yet the Mets responded better than many expected. Green guided the club to a 37-38 record as interim manager. More notably, New York went 31-28 after the All-Star break, entering Tuesday night's game against Texas.

Those numbers hardly establish Green as a proven winner, but they gave the Mets a substantial sample in which to evaluate him. Ownership clearly liked what it saw. " Andy has connected with and pushed our players to perform, despite the disappointment of the season," Steve and Alex Cohen said in a statement.

That is an important distinction. The Mets did not simply promote Green because he had a good few weeks. They spent nearly three months watching him manage the team through a disappointing season and concluded that his approach fit what they wanted moving forward.

His Padres record needs context

Green's lack of playoff appearances is a legitimate part of his résumé, but it also needs context. When he took over the Padres in 2016, San Diego was rebuilding. The organization was focused on developing young talent and constructing a roster capable of competing in the future.

Green's teams went 274-366 during his four seasons, and he was dismissed during the 2019 season. He therefore left San Diego without a winning record or a postseason appearance. Those results cannot simply be erased.

At the same time, managerial records are heavily influenced by the rosters available to a manager. The Padres' eventual emergence as an NL contender came after Green's tenure, underscoring how different the circumstances can be from one managerial job to another.

Green's strongest argument was probably the opportunity the Mets gave him to demonstrate how he would operate their clubhouse. He had nearly three months to establish his expectations, communicate with players and make in-game decisions. New York then had an extended look at him before committing to a three-year contract.

"When I accepted the interim role, I didn't anticipate it becoming permanent," Green said in a statement. "But the more time I spent with our players and staff, the clearer it became that this is where my passion and experience could make the greatest impact." The decision therefore appears less like a bet on Green's past results and more like a bet on the organization’s evaluation of his performance in New York.

That does not make the decision without risk. The Mets are not rebuilding for the sake of rebuilding. A franchise with significant expectations needs a manager capable of navigating a roster built to compete for a postseason spot. Green has never done that as a major-league manager.

His Padres tenure produced four consecutive seasons without October baseball, and his subsequent coaching experience with Arizona and Chicago did not change that part of his résumé. The Mets are now asking him to accomplish something he has never accomplished as a manager. That will make the 2027 season particularly revealing.
